item.title: Version 0.37.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.37.0

  • Let AI agents edit and export your recordings: Claude Code, Codex and other MCP clients can trim, cut words and silences, import media and export through Screendrop (Settings → MCP)
  • Pick the recording area in place: the area stays editable after you draw it, with handles, an exact size or a locked ratio, and Screendrop remembers your last area
  • Cursor styles in Studio: the macOS arrow, four vector arrows and two circles (transparent or frosted), with an inverted look, and a crisp pointing hand that stays sharp in exports
  • A rebuilt Studio timeline: solid, rounded blocks that are easier to grab, move and trim, stop at their neighbours, and land exactly where you draw them, plus a playhead that turns into a flag at the end
  • A new crop for screenshots and videos: handles sit inside the box so they stay easy to grab, drag outside it to start a new selection, nudge with the arrow keys, Shift keeps the ratio and Option resizes from the centre
  • The screenshot editor's canvas now moves without overshooting
  • The Library uses much less memory, and Similar captures load faster
  • Large recordings now upload to Screendrop Cloud in parts, so shares over 100 MB no longer fail. Thanks to @justin-schroeder for the fix!

item.title: Version 0.36.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.36.0

  • Camera layouts: pick from corner, split, fill split and a new Cutout layout that removes your background, with a Layout lane on the Studio timeline
  • Corner camera shrinks out of the way during zooms, and zooms follow the action inside a split
  • Camera touch-ups: face light and skin smoothing
  • Studio now supports text, pixelate, images, GIFs and audio on the timeline, with a resizable, redesigned timeline
  • Cleaner Studio inspector with foldable sections
  • Library v2: a new grid, smart sidebar, on-device text recognition, automatic categories and Similar captures
  • Search Unsplash for frame backgrounds
  • Double-click or press Space on a recording in the Library to open it in the editor
  • Studio exports default to HEVC and run faster
  • Fixed shadows outlining the screen and camera in exports

item.title: Version 0.35.3
item.description:
What's New in 0.35.3

  • Press Space during Capture Area to switch to window selection, just like the system screenshot tool (thanks @Iiviavs)

item.title: Version 0.35.2
item.description:
What's New in 0.35.2

item.title: Version 0.35.1
item.description:
What's New in 0.35.1

  • Fixed the tucked capture shelf handle needing two clicks to reopen, or not reopening at all on some Macs
  • Clicks on the shelf handle that move slightly on a trackpad now open the shelf instead of being ignored

item.title: Version 0.35.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.35.0

  • A redesign of the whole app on one Liquid Glass design system: Settings, Library, the screenshot editor, Studio and every floating panel now share the same controls, and use your Mac's accent color
  • New capture shelf: cards dock to the screen edge, slide in and out through it, and tuck away into a slim handle you can drag anywhere along the edge, so they never cover an editor's buttons
  • Capture cards frost on hover with clearer, equal-width actions, every action is in the right-click menu, and a card can't delete a capture that is open in an editor
  • Studio's sidebar is rebuilt around one short Look: style thumbnails of your own recording, Canvas, Frame, then one switch per feature
  • Pick a background from a single row: hovering a fill previews it on the video or screenshot before you choose
  • The screenshot editor gets Studio's Styles strip, Canvas and Frame sections, and Crop moves into the tool dock, which morphs into the crop bar
  • Annotations now stay on the image: new shapes, moves, resizes and arrow-key nudges stop at its edge
  • The screenshot editor opens on the Select tool, with a Starting tool setting to change it
  • With the sidebar hidden, Share, Save As and Done move to the toolbar instead of floating over the screenshot
  • The teleprompter is now part of the recording bar: its button unfolds the bar into the script editor, with word count and speaking time
  • The recording bar has a grip to drag it anywhere
  • Improved screen and window picker, video timeline and pinhead, and a speed badge for sped-up clips
  • Inspector sections fold smoothly without bouncing, switches are a normal size, and controls dim when they have no effect
  • Error messages now go away on their own
  • Fixed: the watermark section wouldn't open
  • Fixed: Start Recording couldn't be clicked in the source picker
  • Fixed: saving in the editor could drop a card over it
  • Fixed: the pointer flickering on the recording bar

item.title: Version 0.34.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.34.0

  • Faster video exports: every frame now renders on the GPU, the CPU and GPU work on consecutive frames in parallel, HEVC is tuned for encoding speed, and exports no longer run on the main thread, so Studio stays responsive while you export. In our testing, a 50-second camera recording exported up to 40% faster. Actual speedups depend on your Mac, recording, and export settings.
  • An interactive Studio canvas that matches the export: click to play or pause, see the frame you're skimming, drag a Fixed zoom's target right on the paused canvas, and move the camera bubble with snapping guides. The bubble now always stays clear of the canvas edge.
  • A reworked Studio timeline: grouped transport controls, a single current/total time readout, and new shortcuts: ⌘B or S to split at the playhead, arrow keys to step a frame, and Shift-arrow to step a second. Reset Clips now asks for confirmation.
  • A cleaner Studio inspector, consistent with the screenshot editor: timeline selections pinned to the top, collapsed sections with summaries, remembered expanded sections, clip speed presets, and the audio format chosen at export time.
  • A tidier Studio toolbar: a prominent Export button, an icon-only Save, and untitled recordings named by when they were recorded, with length and resolution shown underneath.
  • A refreshed screenshot editor inspector: on/off switches for Border and Watermark, summaries on collapsed sections, and remembered expanded sections.
  • A refined Library window on macOS 27, with a rounded content area beside the sidebar.
  • Fixed a thin dark outline around the corners of rounded screenshot borders, in both the editor and exported images.

item.title: Version 0.33.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.33.0

  • Choose any background color for screenshots and recordings using the new color-picker tile.
  • Adjust recording audio volume from mute to 200%, with changes saved to the project and applied to playback, video exports, and audio-only exports.
  • Show or hide the mouse pointer from the Cursor section in Recording Studio. Hiding the pointer also hides click highlights in preview and export for recordings with a separate cursor track.

item.title: Version 0.32.1
item.description:
What's New in 0.32.1

  • Fixed uneven padding in the recording editor when using Original aspect ratio.
  • Original now fits the cropped video, removing wallpaper strips at 0% padding.
  • Preview and export use matching padding, and older cached exports refresh with the corrected layout.

item.title: Version 0.32.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.32.0

  • Meet the new Media Library: screenshots, videos, and editable recording projects now live in one native macOS window. Browse in grid or list view, search and sort captures, inspect file details, and edit, export, or share from one place.
  • Up to 3× faster video exports with Metal-accelerated rendering. Studio moves demanding motion-blur work to the GPU and reuses unchanged screen frames, with a Core Graphics fallback when needed. Actual speedups depend on your Mac, recording, and export settings.
  • More control over video exports: choose 30 or 60 fps and turn motion blur on or off independently. Your choices are remembered and used consistently for Export, Share, and Library rendering.
  • Smoother annotation navigation: rewritten canvas zoom and pan, pointer-anchored pinch zoom, predictable zoom-out speed, proper canvas boundaries, and a new maximum zoom of 1000%.
  • A visible reminder before recording: when Capture Visibility is enabled, a compact banner below the recorder warns that Screendrop windows will be captured and lets you switch it off immediately.
  • Lower editor memory use: bounded image previews, more efficient rendering resources, and better cleanup when editor windows close. Full-resolution source images and editable screenshot data are preserved.
  • Safer saving: screenshot commits coordinate Save, Done, and Upload, preserve existing files during replacement, and restore them if a save fails. Editors stay open when saving fails, and newer edits are no longer incorrectly marked as saved.
  • Better save recovery: screenshot save failures offer Retry or another destination, and opening a save dialog keeps the preview available even if you cancel. Uploading an untouched screenshot now works too.
  • Countdowns you can cancel: cancel the countdown or close the recorder to stop a pending recording. Source selection is disabled while the countdown is running to prevent duplicate starts.
  • Clearer recording setup: source-loading progress and errors now have visible feedback, a retry action, and a link to screen recording permissions when needed.
  • More reliable shortcuts and Cloud setup: rejected shortcut changes keep the previous working binding and explain the error. Automatic upload settings guide you to Cloud setup when configuration is missing.
  • Cleaner handoffs and more consistent UI: recording preview cards dismiss after successful editor, save, export, and share handoffs; failed or cancelled actions remain available for retry. Library cells, inspector actions, settings labels, and editor controls have been polished throughout.
  • Corrected shadow falloff in perspective screenshot layouts.
  • Screendrop is back under the CC0 1.0 Universal license.

item.title: Version 0.30.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.30.0

  • Screendrop is now a complete, non-destructive screen-recording studio: every recording keeps its screen, camera, audio, pointer, keystroke, and edit data together so you can reopen the project and keep refining it.
  • Edit recordings on a real timeline with thumbnail scrubbing, split, trim, delete, per-clip speed controls, undo and redo, plus a zoomable, scrollable workspace built for long recordings.
  • Turn raw interaction into polished motion with automatic click-driven zooms, editable zoom blocks, pointer-follow reframing, fixed focus points, reconstructed cursor movement, click highlights, and positionable keystroke captions.
  • Record a display, window, or selected area alongside an optional camera, microphone, and system audio; the new pre-record bar adds camera preview, input selection, area highlighting, and 1, 3, or 5 second timers.
  • Present naturally with a notch-native teleprompter that follows your narration using Apple's on-device speech recognition, with a floating fallback for Macs and displays without a notch.
  • Special thanks to Jilles Soeters (@jillesme) for the original idea behind Screendrop's teleprompter.
  • Transcribe narration on-device, fix caption text, burn in karaoke-style word highlighting, or edit the video itself by selecting transcript passages, removing filler words, and trimming narration silences.
  • Compose for every destination with Original, 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, and 4:5 output, Fill or Fit reframing, editable camera placement, backgrounds, padding, corners, shadows, and reusable Studio style presets.
  • Export and Share now render the complete composition-including camera, zooms, cursor, clicks, keystrokes, captions, clip edits, speed changes, and selected audio-with progress, cancellation, completion feedback, and render reuse when nothing changed.
  • Annotation Studio has a new unified shape engine, a Highlight tool, reusable background presets, a refined inspector, and full-resolution wide-gamut exports that better match the on-screen preview.
  • Create richer screenshot mockups with perspective camera controls, zoom and pan, progressive radial or directional blur, configurable edge behavior, solid borders, wallpapers, gradients, watermarks, alignment, padding, corner radius, and shadow.
  • Open one or many images from Finder directly in Screendrop; each image is imported as an editable copy in History, leaving the original untouched.
  • Automate screenshots and recordings through Apple Shortcuts, Siri, and Spotlight, and choose whether Screendrop's own windows appear in captures from Settings.
  • Cloud sharing gains upload titles, comments and likes controls, richer video sidecars for posters, transcripts, and scrub previews, plus the ability to delete an uploaded capture from History and invalidate its public link.
  • Polish and reliability are everywhere: smoother preview-card animations, faster off-main screenshot rendering, cached wallpaper previews, more reliable click capture without Input Monitoring, better teleprompter placement on external displays, and extensive recording-toolbar, timeline, cursor, zoom, and export fixes.

item.title: Version 0.21.1
item.description:
What's New in 0.21.1

  • Fixed a glitch where preview cards briefly looked square (the image overflowed the rounded corners) while the overlay collapsed or expanded.

item.title: Version 0.21.0
item.description:
What's New in 0.21.0

  • New peek tab: recent captures now collapse into a compact pill at the bottom of the screen while you edit or preview, instead of disappearing. Click it to bring your stack back, or scroll down to tuck it away.
  • Quick Look (press Space) now keeps your captures in the peek tab instead of hiding the overlay.
  • Crop tool: crop and reframe your screenshots right inside the annotator.
  • Clear all captures at once with the new button on the peek tab.
  • Unsaved capture warning: Screendrop now warns you before quitting or updating when you have captures that haven't been saved to disk, so you never lose work.
  • Smoother, single-axis overlay animations and refined peek-pill visuals.
  • Various annotator polish for buttons and labels.

item.title: Version 0.20.3

What's New in 0.20.3

item.title: Version 0.20.2
item.description:

item.title: Version 0.20.1
item.description:
What's New in 0.20.1

item.title: Version 0.20
item.description:
What's New in 0.20

  • Double-click to edit - Double-click a preview card to jump straight into the editor (annotator for images, video editor for recordings). First community contribution, thanks @jamesqquick! 🎉
  • Upload from the annotator - A new Upload action in the annotation editor saves your annotations, uploads the full-resolution image to your cloud, and copies the link to your clipboard - without closing the editor. Shows a live progress spinner and a "Link copied" confirmation.
  • Low-resolution editor preview - The annotator uses a lighter preview to keep memory usage down on large captures. It's now an explicit setting (Settings → Screenshots → Annotation Editor, on by default), the preview is sharper than before, and a small info badge in the editor explains it. Exports are always full resolution.
  • Redesigned annotation editor toolbar - Save As, Done, and Upload now live in a native macOS Liquid Glass toolbar pill with consistent iconography, replacing the old sidebar button bar.
  • Smoother stacked-preview behavior - cards dismiss horizontally and overflow is trimmed more gracefully.
  • Removed the legacy capture-hide flow for a snappier capture path.
  • The floating preview overlay no longer sits on top of the annotation editor, video editor, or Quick Look - it hides while those are open and reliably returns afterward (fixes cases where it blocked clicks/scrolling).

item.title: Version 0.19
item.description:
What's New in 0.19

  • Zoom images in annotator
  • Smart redaction and blur feature

item.title: Version 0.18
item.description:
What's New in 0.18

item.title: Version 0.7
item.description:
What's New in 0.7

  • After-capture actions - Choose exactly what happens after a screenshot or recording (independently): show the preview overlay, copy, save, upload to Cloud & copy link, open the editor, or pin. Set them up in Settings → Screenshots and Settings → Video.
  • Pin to screen - Keep a screenshot floating on top for reference. Pin from the preview card, then drag it anywhere; hover for copy/save/close.
  • Copy text from image (OCR) - Right-click a screenshot in the preview or a pinned window to copy any text in it.
  • Self-timer - Add a 3, 5, or 10-second countdown before a capture (Settings → Screenshots).
  • Color picker - Pick a color anywhere on screen from the menu bar; the hex is copied to your clipboard.
  • Overlay preferences - Choose which corner the preview docks to, auto-close it after a delay, and toggle close-after-drag.
  • Capture options - Mute capture sounds, hide the menu bar icon, and optionally include a window's shadow when capturing a window.

item.title: Version 0.16
item.description:
What's New in 0.16

  • Smoother arrow curving - Bending arrows is now twice as responsive, and arrows snap back to a straight line when you drag the curve near the center.
  • Redesigned background picker - Backgrounds, gradients, solid colors, and wallpapers now share one clean, consistent grid with a clear selection highlight. Default padding and corner rounding have been toned down.

item.title: Version 0.15
item.description:
What's New in 0.15

  • Non-destructive annotations. Edits are no longer flattened permanently - screenshots keep their original pixels and a re-editable .screendrop sidecar, so you can reopen and tweak annotations any time after saving.
  • Smarter clipboard & saving. After editing, the latest version is automatically re-copied to the clipboard and the existing saved file is overwritten in place - no more stale copies or duplicate files.
  • Cloud setup is much smoother. A secure upload token is generated for you (with Copy / Reveal / Regenerate), and Verify Connection now provisions your worker's database automatically - no manual migration step after a one-click deploy.
  • Worker update notifications. The app detects when your deployed Cloud worker is behind and shows a non-blocking "update available" notice with a how-to link.
  • Cloud settings redesign. Cleaner, less cluttered layout with native input fields, an inline token reveal, and a collapsible setup guide.

item.title: Version 0.1
item.description:
What's New in 0.1

  • Capture fullscreen, window, or custom area screenshots with global hotkeys (Option+1/2/3)
  • Annotate screenshots with rectangles, ellipses, arrows, freehand drawing, text, numbered circles, and pixelate/blur tools
  • Floating preview panel with screenshot stack for quick access to recent captures
  • Auto-copy to clipboard, auto-save to disk, and optional JPEG compression
